title: Gateway lease renewal leak led to slow reclaim and tenant 429 microbursts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: During a rolling deployment of gateway-2.9.1 we observed repeated short-duration 429 spikes affecting a subset of tenants in us-east-1. The traffic pattern looked like synchronized microbursts: a set of clients would immediately receive 429s for ~30–90s then recover. This caused several customer escalations and transient SLA breaches. This ticket captures the investigation, root cause, short-term mitigations, and a prioritized action plan to prevent recurrence.
detection: On 2026-02-09 22:14 UTC alerting paged on elevated 429-rate for api.gateway.prod in us-east-1. SRE dashboards showed correlated increase in token_unavailable logs and lease_reassign warnings. Eng on-call began triage and created incident INC-2026-0210.
timeline: 2026-02-09 22:08 UTC: Canary deployment of gateway-2.9.1 started in us-east-1.
2026-02-09 22:14 UTC: 429-rate alert triggered (5m rolling avg +3x baseline) affecting ~120 tenants.
2026-02-09 22:20 UTC: On-call SRE identified spike coincident with gateway pod restarts and Redis lease TTL anomalies.
2026-02-09 22:33 UTC: Rapid rollback initiated to gateway-2.9.0; 429 rates reduced to baseline by 22:45 UTC.
2026-02-10 00:10 UTC: After rollback, deeper logs analyzed; found lease entries without TTL were being reissued across tenant namespaces.
2026-02-11 09:00 UTC: Reproduction in staging with scaled synthetic client confirmed race between lease reaper and new-lease path.
2026-02-16 15:30 UTC: Patch implementing atomic SETEX via Lua script merged (PR #4876) and deployed to canary with no regressions observed.
2026-02-17 10:00 UTC: Postmortem draft created and initial action items assigned.
root_cause: A race condition in the Redis-backed token lease allocation path allowed expired lease keys (keys left without TTL by an earlier fast-fail code path) to be re-read and re-assigned to different tenants before the reaper cleaned them. The new gateway code in 2.9.1 introduced a path that performed a GET then separate SET without an atomic TTL set, making it possible for a concurrent reassign to read a stale value and cause quota misattribution. Combined factors: (1) sliding-window token bucket change that reduced margins for race windows, (2) an earlier bug that left some keys without TTL under specific failure mode, and (3) rolling deploy timing that produced synchronized lease churn across pods.
mitigations: Immediate: Rolled back gateway-2.9.1 to 2.9.0 in affected region; restored baseline SLA within ~30m.
Short-term: Deployed hotfix that uses a Lua script to perform GET+SETEX atomically (PR #4876) and increases lease-reaper frequency in us-east-1 by 2x.
Monitoring: Added metric lease_ttl_missing_count and alert when >100 in 5m; added tag-forwarding for tenant_id on lease operations to speed triage.
Customer comms: Notified impacted customers via status page and opened priority support tickets for high-importance tenants.
action_items: ENG-119101: Replace all non-atomic GET+SET lease codepaths with Lua SETEX scripts and add unit tests (owner: Tomas Rivera, estimate: 3, due: 2026-02-24).
ENG-119102: Add e2e chaos test in staging that simulates rolling restarts + Redis slow responses to catch lease races (owner: Maya Chen, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-03).
ENG-119103: Harden deploy canary policy to sequenced, not parallel, across gateway replicas in a region (owner: SRE Team, estimate: 2, due: 2026-02-28).
ENG-119104: Audit all Redis codepaths for TTL guarantees; create linter rule to flag SET without expiry for lease-like keys (owner: Security/Infra, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-10).
ENG-119105: Update runbook and playbook with troubleshooting steps for lease misallocation and include quick remediation commands (owner: Aisha Kapoor, estimate: 1, due: 2026-02-20).
ENG-119106: Add synthetic customer-surface load test that asserts no tenant-level 429s during rolling deploys (owner: Load-Team, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-15).
ENG-119107: Post-deploy canary threshold: require stable lease_ttl_missing_count < 5 for 15m before promoting (owner: Deploy Safety, estimate: 1, due: 2026-02-18).
testing_and_validation: Reproduced in staging by injecting 200ms Redis latency and performing concurrent lease allocations from 500 synthetic clients; observed same race without Lua SETEX, resolved when using the Lua script.
Canary of hotfix deployed to us-east-1 (3% of traffic) for 12 hours with no 429 regressions; then promoted globally.
Added unit tests for lease reassign and integration tests against redis-mock verifying TTL present on success and cleared on error paths.
risks_and_followups: Risk: Other services that implement lease-like patterns may have similar non-atomic sets. We need an org-wide sweep.
Follow-up: Schedule a 1-week audit sprint to find and remediate non-atomic Redis usage across infra (see ENG-119104).
Follow-up: Consider migrating critical lease store to Redis Streams or a small bounded in-memory RAFT cluster for stronger ownership guarantees (investigate Q2).
notes: Operational note: The race window was small (<200ms) which is why only a subset of tenants exposed the issue depending on client timing and pod placement.
Engineering note: The Lua SETEX approach adds a tiny CPU cost but removes the class of races; acceptable trade for critical lease keys.
SRE suggestion: Add a temporary mitigation of a short client-side randomized backoff when receiving 429s during deploy windows to reduce synchronized retry storms.
final_status: Hotfix merged and promoted globally; action items opened with owners assigned. Pending org-wide Redis atomicity audit.
